body:
Enumerated after fixing the importer half of F-7e418c, to find out whether that
fix was complete. It is not, and the reason is structural rather than a missing
line.

## Every writer of ub.Annotation, and whether it sets the column

    cps/annotations.py:424          Kobo sqlite importer      SETS IT (F-7e418c fix)
    cps/annotations.py:981          web reader, unanchored note   no
    cps/annotations.py:1014         web reader, CFI-only          no
    cps/annotations.py:1041         web reader, kobospan-anchored no
    cps/services/annotation_portable.py:131  KOReader portable import  no
    cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:289  live Kobo PATCH   SETS IT, conditionally

Two of six set it. One of those two only when the payload happens to carry a
`type` key.

## Why the remaining four are NOT a missing line

**The web reader has no type vocabulary.** It distinguishes a highlight from a
note purely by whether `note_text` is populated — `frontend/src/pages/Reader.tsx`
does exactly that, and there is no `'note'` token anywhere in `cps/`. So setting
`annotation_type = "note"` for the unanchored-note path, or `"highlight"` for the
other two, would invent tokens this system has never used. That is precisely the
mistake `cps/services/annotation_colors.py` exists to undo for `highlight_color`,
where three vocabularies accumulated in one column and had to be reconciled after
the fact.

The importer fix was safe only because it does NOT choose a value: it copies
`Bookmark.Type` verbatim, and the device's word and the wire payload's word are
already the same ("highlight", evidenced by the KOReader plugin writing
`Type = "highlight"` and selecting `WHERE Type = 'highlight'`, plus two protocol
fixtures).

**The portable path has nothing to copy.** `annotation_portable.py` never
mentions the column in either direction, so a KOReader export -> import round trip
cannot preserve a type it was never given. Fixing that means extending the plugin
protocol, not editing the importer.

## The actual root cause

The column was added by #1685 as "Stage 0 two-way-sync metadata" and no writer
was made responsible for it. It is read today only by
`cps/services/kobo_annotation_stage0.py`, a field list — so nothing user-visible
depends on it yet, and nothing has forced the vocabulary question to be answered.

That is the decision that has to be made before the remaining writers can be
fixed honestly: **what is the agreed set of values, and who owns it?** Once that
exists, the four remaining writers are mechanical.

## Recommended shape, not implemented

Mirror what was done for colour: one module that owns the vocabulary, converts
in both directions, refuses to invent a value it does not know, and refuses to
destroy a token it does not recognise. Then have every writer route through it.
Doing that for a column nothing reads yet is cheap; doing it after two-way sync
ships is the `annotation_colors.py` cleanup all over again.

## Do not "fix" this with a backfill first

Backfilling a vocabulary that has not been agreed writes the guess into the data,
where it is much harder to retract than a line of code. Forward agreement first.

resolution.note: Fixed in #1760 (+#1777): cps/services/annotation_types.py is now the declared owner, and all six ub.Annotation constructors route through it -- importer and portable import and live PATCH via to_storage_type, the three web-reader paths via type_for_webreader_annotation. The vocabulary question this finding said had to be answered first IS answered in that module's docstring: highlight/dogear are the device's own words, note is declared web-reader-only, unknown words survive rather than being nulled or defaulted. Guarded by a source-scanning enumeration test plus a vacuity control (test_the_scan_finds_the_constructors_it_claims_to). Mutation re-verified 2026-08-22.

title: annotation_type has five writers, no owner, and no agreed vocabulary
